plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has told several times about Hanford in Washington state, a site that made plutonium for the first atomic bombs. Drawing on the researcher Robert Hastings and his book on UFOs and nuclear weapons, Michels says that in 1945, months before the first atomic test and the bombings of Japan, a man named Bud Clem, whom Michels in one telling calls a pilot, described glowing balls of light hovering over the site, and that jet fighters chased them without success. In other tellings he ties the sightings to an Air Force study he calls Project Twinkle, which he says was deleted from Air Force archives, or credits a Lieutenant Commander Brown instead of Clem, and he tells it because it would suggest unknown objects were watching nuclear sites from the very start.
